title: "Checkpoint evaluation: from ladder loss to usable-model evidence"
subtitle: "Fixed holdouts, task protocols, exports, recurrence parity and automatic records"
date: 2026-11-02

## Evaluation is part of the trainer qualification

Build the evaluator before large ladder runs. It must answer three questions: is the training computation correct; which recipe improves the fixed target distribution; and does the model acquire the capabilities we care about? Training loss alone cannot answer all three, especially when data mixtures change.

The [TorchTitan validation guide](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/blob/1d1fa9444d07b79351c9ed660b3ac4a5f52dfef9/docs/evaluation.md) separates in-loop validation from external task evaluation after checkpoint conversion. Megatron likewise has in-loop validation and distributed checkpointing; a training checkpoint is not automatically a Hugging Face model. The [LM Evaluation Harness](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness) is downloaded at commit `d6de81643928d653435c431bae19945d41d32520`; its tracked source is archived in `references/evaluation/2026-lm-evaluation-harness/`.

## Freeze a three-level suite

| Level | Proposed use | Measurements and controls |
|---|---|---|
| Numerical fixtures | Every trainer/export/loop change | Logits, masked NLL, gradients, optimizer step and full-forward/cache parity on known token IDs |
| Fixed distribution losses | Every selected checkpoint in every ladder run | Held-out web quality bands, code, math, scientific text, cyber domain; token-weighted NLL plus BPB where useful |
| Downstream capability tasks | Milestones and all final annealed endpoints | Fixed task versions, few-shot settings, prompts, extraction rules, accuracy/normalized accuracy/exact match and uncertainty |

Proposed cheap task slice: HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC-Easy/Challenge and WinoGrande. Proposed fuller milestones: MMLU, GSM8K and a carefully versioned code-generation benchmark, plus internally held-out cyber tasks. These are candidate evaluation choices, not a claim that every task has statistical power at tiny proxy sizes. Use published task configurations from the pinned harness; audit dataset versions and access before freezing names.

Tiny models often score near chance. Keep continuous choice log-likelihood/margin or domain BPB available, and do not select a mixture solely on chance-level task accuracy. AI2's task-scaling report in [our library](../../references/evaluation/2024-ai2-task-scaling-model-ladders/paper.pdf) explicitly motivates separating language-model/task loss from bounded accuracy prediction.

## Define loss precisely

For fixed held-out token positions $\mathcal V$, model conditional probabilities $p_\theta$, and binary loss mask $m_i$,

$$
\mathrm{NLL}_{\rm tok}=-\frac{\sum_{i\in\mathcal V}m_i\log p_\theta(x_i\mid x_{<i})}{\sum_{i\in\mathcal V}m_i}.
$$

Exclude padding and declared context-only positions. Record whether EOS is scored, whether documents share context and how long-document windows overlap. Average total loss sums and token counts across ranks; an unweighted average of microbatch means can bias results when token counts differ. Router regularizers are training diagnostics and should not be silently included in held-out next-token NLL.

For the same raw UTF-8 evaluation text,

$$
\mathrm{BPB}=\frac{-\sum_i\log p_\theta(x_i\mid x_{<i})}{\ln2\;n_{\rm bytes}}.
$$

State text normalization, byte accounting, document boundary conditioning and special-token scoring. BPB permits comparison across tokenizers only when raw text and scoring semantics are comparable. Do not call BPB “BPC”: Farseer uses a character denominator, whereas Marin's records report bytes. They differ on Unicode text.

Freeze domain weights $v_b$ before comparing mixtures: $L_{\rm target}=\sum_bv_bL_b$. Training runs may use different training weights $w_b$, but the evaluator's $v_b$ stays fixed. A lower own-mixture training loss may merely mean sampling easier text.

## Protect model selection from leakage

Create three boundaries: training data; development evaluation used for recipe selection; and final held-out tasks/slices used only for acceptance. Remove benchmark-derived training documents before tokenization/export. Split duplicate and synthetic-parent families together. Check evaluation paths and checksums as carefully as training manifests.

Use paired item differences for checkpoint/recipe comparisons and paired run seeds where possible. Bootstrap independent documents/items or run families, not correlated tokens from one paragraph. When many mixtures are screened, rerun finalists with fresh seeds and a held-out slice. Sibling cooldown branches sharing a prefix should remain in the same fold of surrogate cross-validation.

The Marin legacy records store `n_eval_tasks`, effective sample counts and several grouped BPB objectives. Different task coverage can move macro means even without a model improvement. Recompute scores from the same common task set before comparing rows; do not rank unlike macro averages blindly.

## Checkpoint lifecycle and cadence

Our proposed default is lightweight fixed-loss validation every 1–2% of training tokens, cheap tasks at roughly 10% milestones, and the full suite at phase boundaries and fully annealed endpoints. Adjust frequency after measuring evaluation overhead. At tiny proxy scales, final-only fuller tasks may be more efficient. Checkpoint frequency for fault recovery is a separate wall-time decision.

Use an explicit lifecycle:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["Checkpoint writing"] --> B["All shards complete + manifest checksums"]
    B --> C["Immutable ready marker"]
    C --> D["Native fixed-loss evaluation"]
    C --> E["Model-specific export and numerical parity"]
    E --> F["External harness and generation tasks"]
    D --> G["Results keyed by checkpoint + eval protocol hash"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["Target score, guardrails, uncertainty and acceptance"]
```

Retries must be idempotent: the same checkpoint/protocol hash maps to the same result key. Missing shards, a still-writing checkpoint or a failed export must produce failure status rather than an empty score. Store task-level outputs and enough metadata to rerun the measurement. Avoid loading a checkpoint while an asynchronous save is incomplete.

## Native validation configuration

In the inspected TorchTitan version, configure `Validator.Config(freq=..., steps=..., dataloader=...)` in a Python recipe. Its default can use C4 validation; **replace that with our immutable holdouts**. The guide supports `repeat=False`, permitting complete finite evaluation. Training and validation should have separate sampler state.

In Megatron, the example uses `--eval-interval` and `--eval-iters`; these are updates and batches, not tokens or a declaration of a fixed full evaluation set. Convert to loss-bearing token coverage and ensure repeated evaluations select the intended identical holdout. Inspect the pinned training evaluator and token-weighted loss tests before relying on its aggregation for packed variable-length data.

If external evaluation borrows hero GPUs, count that time in the budget. A separate asynchronous worker avoids stalls but is additional compute, not free capacity.

## Export and independent evaluator parity

For a **supported standard Llama3 8B**, TorchTitan's pinned converter exposes this illustrative interface:

```bash
cd /mnt/shared/repos/scaling-ladder-knowledge/tmp/torchtitan
python scripts/checkpoint_conversion/convert_to_hf.py \
  /checkpoints/standard-llama3/step-1000 \
  /eval-models/standard-llama3-step-1000 \
  --hf_assets_path /datasets/llama3-8b-assets \
  --model_name llama3 --model_flavor 8B --export_dtype bfloat16
```

These are placeholder paths; this command has not been executed. The converter's defaults and model registry are architecture-specific. Preserve the correct tokenizer and supply an architecture-matching `config.json`; weight serialization does not synthesize a correct arbitrary custom model definition.

For Megatron, use the selected release's compatible model-specific conversion tooling or a tested native harness adapter. The repository's GPT-OSS examples demonstrate a particular conversion route, not a universal converter for a new MoE. Obtain a known standard checkpoint, round-trip it and compare logits before exporting our own architecture.

TorchTitan's conversion README recommends greedy-decoding checks and a distributional/KL test; it illustrates how a missing RoPE permutation can produce subtle errors. Adopt both, with measured precision-dependent tolerances on fixed inputs. Also compare held-out NLL and token IDs. Passing a shape check or producing fluent output is insufficient.

For the proposed repeated middle blocks, create a custom model definition or native adapter that executes shared weights in the correct order and maintains **separate KV cache entries per visit**. Compare cached generation to full-prefix recomputation. Do not label its weights as a standard non-looped Qwen/Llama configuration. Until this path passes, external scores are not trustworthy.

## Harness invocation and task controls

In a separate evaluation environment built from the pinned harness, a **standard supported HF model** can be tested with:

```bash
lm_eval --model hf \
  --model_args pretrained=/eval-models/standard-model,dtype=bfloat16 \
  --tasks hellaswag --num_fewshot 0 --batch_size 8 \
  --output_path /eval-results/standard-model/hellaswag \
  --log_samples
```

Run 0-shot ARC/PIQA/WinoGrande as separately frozen tasks or a documented group; run 5-shot MMLU and the chosen GSM8K few-shot protocol separately. A single global `num_fewshot` should not accidentally overwrite different intended protocols. Pin task YAMLs, dataset revisions, harness seed, tokenizer, maximum context, generation stop strings, temperature and answer parser. Base-model evaluation should not silently add an instruction chat template.

A vLLM backend may accelerate supported models, but custom recurrent MoE support requires separate model/cache integration. Use a native scorer or qualified HF backend first. Tool/code execution benchmarks need a controlled execution environment; their result is not interchangeable with multiple-choice code knowledge.

## Result record and acceptance

Every result should contain the run/config hash, corpus release, checkpoint token count, stored/active/executed parameter counts, training seed, phase and decay status, evaluator commit, task/data revision, token/byte counts, per-domain NLL/BPB, task metrics with uncertainty, throughput and errors. Keep full task metrics alongside the aggregate.

A proposed acceptance gate is: no fixture/export/cache failure; no unresolved contamination; a positive paired improvement on the predeclared target objective; and no material regression on critical capability/domain guardrails beyond measured noise. Set the actual tolerance before seeing finalists. Compare fully annealed endpoints at matched exposure and also wall-clock quality, since a slower recurrent model may lose a nominal FLOP advantage.

No checkpoint evaluation has been run here. This guide defines the integration and evidence needed to evaluate the future ladder and hero run consistently.
